map.subsystem: CI security gates (GitHub Actions security/lint/dependency gates, CodeRabbit pre-merge checks, external secret scanning, and the documented not-doing decisions) — repo android-unofficial

capabilities.name: Required status check roster
capabilities.behavior: Five gates are required on `develop` via the "Protect develop" ruleset (docs/dev/security-testing.md:31): exact check names `Security Scan Gate`, `Dependency Scan Gate`, `Workflow Lint`, `Workflow Security`, `Android Gate`. Check name = the job's `name:`, not the workflow's `name:`. Non-required additional jobs that report their own status: `Detect Dependency Changes`, `OSV-Scanner`, `Detect Android-Relevant Changes`, `Build & Test`, `Instrumented Tests (emulator)`, `App Token Auth + Runner Check`, `Attribution Check`. None of the five required gates uses `continue-on-error`. `Security Scan Gate`, `Workflow Lint`, `Workflow Security` run unconditionally on every PR; `Android Gate` and `Dependency Scan Gate` are always-running aggregation jobs (`if: always()`) that pass when no relevant paths changed and fail closed otherwise.
edge_cases: A paths-filtered required job would never be created and would wedge the merge as "pending" — this is the stated reason workflow-security.yml has no PR paths filter (workflow-security.yml:29-33) and security-scan.yml has no detect-changes fan-out (security-scan.yml:14-16).

CONTRIBUTING.md:265-274 is stale: it lists only 5 checks, describes `Workflow Lint` as "zizmor static analysis … (advisory while it beds in)" (actually actionlint, and failing), and says Security Scan Gate runs "against the diff" (actually whole directories). docs/dev/security-testing.md is the accurate source.

capabilities.name: Security Scan Gate — Semgrep SAST job shape
capabilities.behavior: Workflow `Security Scan` (.github/workflows/security-scan.yml). Triggers: push to main/develop; pull_request to main/develop on opened|synchronize|reopened; workflow_dispatch. `permissions: contents: read`. Concurrency group `security-scan-${{ github.ref }}`, cancel-in-progress true. Single job `security-scan-gate` / name `Security Scan Gate`, runs-on ubuntu-latest, `timeout-minutes: 10`. Deliberately one job with no detect-changes fan-out so the required status always reports. Steps: checkout (persist-credentials false) → `pip install semgrep==1.169.0` → run scan capturing exit code into `SEMGREP_EXIT` via GITHUB_ENV → upload artifact (`if: always()`) → gate step. The CLI is pinned but the p/kotlin, p/java, p/secrets rule packs are fetched from the Semgrep registry at scan time, so rule content can move between runs.
edge_cases: Rule-pack drift means a previously-green commit can turn red with no repo change.

capabilities.name: Semgrep scan invocation and scope
capabilities.behavior: `semgrep scan --config p/kotlin --config p/java --config p/secrets --exclude 'AesEcb.java' --exclude '.gradle' --json --output semgrep-kotlin.json app/ wear-device/ watchface/ plugins/ tools/`. Exit code is captured with `|| EXIT=$?` so the step itself never fails. Scanned roots: app/, wear-device/, watchface/, plugins/, tools/. `tools/` (the medtronic-ble-spike Sake crypto reverse-engineering) is deliberately IN scope so SAST coverage matches the dependency scan, which already covers its lockfile. Non-shipped spikes under tools/ fall outside only the CodeRabbit `plugins/shipped/**/ble/**` path rules; CodeRabbit's semantic BLE Protocol Safety custom check still applies to them.
edge_cases: docs/dev/security-testing.md:222-228 local-repro snippet omits `tools/` from the target list — the local command scans less than CI.

capabilities.name: Semgrep exclusions and their rationale
capabilities.behavior: Two excludes. (1) `AesEcb.java` — vendored from OpenMinimed JavaSake, re-vendored rather than patched on upstream bumps (issues #695/#696), so its intentional legacy AES/ECB usage must never fail the gate. JavaSake is currently consumed as the Maven artifact `org.openminimed:javasake` with no vendored source in-tree, so the exclusion is INERT TODAY and retained only for the re-vendor case. (2) `.gradle` — Gradle build cache, never source. The exclude is a bare basename pattern, so any file named AesEcb.java anywhere in the tree is skipped.
edge_cases: Basename-scoped exclusion: an unrelated future AesEcb.java would also be silently unscanned.

capabilities.name: Semgrep pass/fail threshold and fail-closed
capabilities.behavior: Two-part gate on semgrep-kotlin.json. (a) Scanner-error fail-closed: `if [ "${SEMGREP_EXIT:-2}" -ge 2 ]` → `::error::` + exit 1. Semgrep exit 1 means "findings produced" (normal); ≥2 means the scanner itself errored. The `:-2` default means a missing/unset SEMGREP_EXIT also fails. (b) Severity threshold: `HIGH = jq '[.results[] | select(.extra.severity == "ERROR" or == "HIGH" or == "CRITICAL")] | length'`. If HIGH > 0, it prints each as `[HIGH] <last dotted segment of check_id> <path>:<start.line> -- <first 160 chars of extra.message>` and exits 1. WARNING findings are counted into `WARN` and printed as non-blocking; INFO is neither counted nor blocking. Mirrors the monorepo's evaluate-sast.py policy.
edge_cases: `jq` on a missing/empty semgrep-kotlin.json would make the gate step error out — also a fail-closed outcome.
No suppression/baseline file exists for Semgrep; the only escape hatch is a `nosemgrep` comment or an added --exclude.

capabilities.name: Semgrep unparseable-file surfacing (non-blocking)
capabilities.behavior: Semgrep records unparseable files in `.errors[]` WITHOUT bumping its exit code, so silently dropped findings would leave no signal. The gate step computes `PARSE = jq '[.errors[]? | select((.type == "Syntax error") or (.type[0]? == "PartialParsing"))] | length'` — matching BOTH schema forms: the string type `"Syntax error"` and the array form `["PartialParsing", ...]` that this Semgrep version emits. If PARSE > 0 it emits `::warning::Semgrep could not parse N file(s)` and lists `.path // .location.path // "?"` sorted-unique. This is visibility only; PASS/FAIL policy is unchanged (block only on ERROR-severity results plus scanner exit ≥ 2).
edge_cases: A Kotlin file that fails to parse is scanned as zero findings and still passes the gate.

capabilities.name: Semgrep result artifact
capabilities.behavior: `actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a` (v7.0.1), `if: always()`, artifact name `semgrep-kotlin`, path `semgrep-kotlin.json`, `if-no-files-found: warn`, `retention-days: 30`. This artifact plus the run log plus CodeRabbit is the entire finding-surfacing mechanism — there is no issue-filing pipeline.
edge_cases: `if-no-files-found: warn` means a crashed scanner that wrote no JSON still uploads nothing without failing the upload step; the gate step catches it.

capabilities.name: Dependency Scan Gate — three-job structure
capabilities.behavior: Workflow `Dependency Vulnerability Scan` (dependency-scan.yml). Triggers: push main/develop; pull_request main/develop; `schedule: cron '0 6 * * 1'` (weekly Monday 06:00 UTC, to catch newly disclosed CVEs); workflow_dispatch. Permissions `contents: read` + `pull-requests: read` (for dorny/paths-filter on PR runs). Concurrency `dep-scan-${{ github.ref }}`, cancel-in-progress true. Jobs: `detect-changes` (name "Detect Dependency Changes") → `scan` (name "OSV-Scanner") → `dep-scan-gate` (name "Dependency Scan Gate", `needs: [detect-changes, scan]`, `if: always()`). `scan` runs only if `should_scan == 'true'` OR event is schedule OR workflow_dispatch.
edge_cases: No `timeout-minutes` on any job in this workflow.

capabilities.name: Dependency scan path filter
capabilities.behavior: `dorny/paths-filter@7b450fff21473bca461d4b92ce414b9d0420d706` (v4.0.2), filter id `deps`, output wired to `should_scan`. Matched globs: `**/build.gradle.kts`, `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, `**/gradle.lockfile`, `settings-gradle.lockfile`, `osv-scanner.toml`, `.github/workflows/dependency-scan.yml`. Intent: any file that can change the resolved dependency graph — build scripts, version catalog, a lockfile, the suppression config — or the workflow itself, re-runs the scan.
edge_cases: `gradle/**` is NOT in this filter (only `gradle/libs.versions.toml`), unlike android.yml which uses `gradle/**`.
A newly disclosed CVE against unchanged deps is caught only by the weekly cron or a manual dispatch, not by an unrelated PR.

capabilities.name: OSV-Scanner install and invocation
capabilities.behavior: Installed from source on the runner's preinstalled Go toolchain — no third-party action to pin: `go install github.com/google/osv-scanner/v2/cmd/osv-scanner@v2.3.3`, then `$HOME/go/bin` appended to GITHUB_PATH. Run: `osv-scanner scan --lockfile=gradle.lockfile:settings-gradle.lockfile --recursive --no-ignore --config=osv-scanner.toml .`. `--recursive` auto-discovers every gradle.lockfile in the tree. The root `settings-gradle.lockfile` has a non-standard basename so it needs the explicit `gradle.lockfile:` parse-as hint. `--no-ignore` stops --recursive from honoring .gitignore, so a future lockfile-matching ignore rule or a moved module cannot silently drop a lockfile while the gate stays green; the CI checkout contains only committed files (no build/ dirs), so there is no over-scan risk. Threshold: any known vulnerability → non-zero exit → gate fails. No severity floor.
edge_cases: docs/dev/security-testing.md:236-241 local-repro command omits `--no-ignore` — local reproduction can scan fewer lockfiles than CI.

capabilities.name: Dependency Scan Gate aggregation logic
capabilities.behavior: `dep-scan-gate` reads DETECT_RESULT, SHOULD_SCAN, SCAN_RESULT, EVENT_NAME from `needs.*` into env and decides: (1) `DETECT_RESULT != success` → exit 1. (2) event is `schedule` or `workflow_dispatch` → require `SCAN_RESULT == success`, else exit 1 (never skips). (3) push/PR with `SHOULD_SCAN != 'true'` → print "No dependency changes -- skipped", exit 0. (4) `SCAN_RESULT == success` → exit 0. (5) otherwise (failure OR cancelled) → exit 1. Values are passed through `env:` rather than interpolated into the shell, which is the template-injection-safe pattern zizmor enforces.
edge_cases: A skipped `scan` job yields SCAN_RESULT == 'skipped', which branch (3) turns into a pass — intended.
On a PR that changes only app code, the dependency gate passes without scanning anything.

capabilities.name: osv-scanner.toml suppression policy
capabilities.behavior: Ships with NO active `[[IgnoredVulns]]` entries. Documented first-scan triage: osv-scanner v2.3.3 across every committed Gradle lockfile (app/, wear-device/, watchface/, plugins/**, tools/medtronic-ble-spike/, settings-gradle.lockfile) reported zero known vulnerabilities across ~1,175 resolved packages. Policy: prefer bumping the dependency or its version-catalog pin; suppress only when there is no upstream fix and the code path is genuinely unreachable. Every entry requires a written `reason`. Documented escape hatch for a CVE fixable only by an AGP bump: `[[IgnoredVulns]] id = "GHSA-..."; ignoreUntil = 2026-12-31T00:00:00Z; reason = "…; tracked in #NNN."` — the `ignoreUntil` forces re-evaluation. Suppressions are reviewed quarterly.
edge_cases: Because androidx/AGP-managed artifacts are scanned, a CVE fixable only by an AGP bump can turn the gate red before the bump lands.

capabilities.name: Gradle dependency locking (what the dep gate actually reads)
capabilities.behavior: OSV-Scanner does not parse build.gradle.kts or libs.versions.toml; coverage exists only because `allprojects { dependencyLocking { lockAllConfigurations() } }` in build.gradle.kts commits a gradle.lockfile per module. Two configuration families are excluded from locking via `excludedFromLocking(name)` = `name.startsWith("_internal-unified-test-platform") || name.endsWith("DependenciesMetadata")`, applied by `resolutionStrategy.deactivateDependencyLocking()`. Reasons: AGP's bundled instrumented-test host tooling (netty, protobuf) is version-pinned by AGP, never ships in an APK, and can only move via an AGP bump — locking it would put AGP's internal supply chain on the CVE gate with unfixable findings; `*DependenciesMetadata` are Kotlin compile-metadata views, not real classpaths. Everything else, including other `_agp_internal_*` configurations, stays locked and scanned.
edge_cases: The `:watchface` lockfile is legitimately empty — resource-only Watch Face Format module with no dependencies.

Renovate runs in a container without the Android SDK and cannot regenerate Android lockfiles; regen-gradle-lockfiles.yml refreshes them on Renovate Gradle PRs and pushes back. That path is UNPROVEN — Renovate is not yet configured on this repository.

capabilities.name: resolveAndLockAll task (lockfile completeness check)
capabilities.behavior: Registered per-project in build.gradle.kts. `notCompatibleWithConfigurationCache`. `doFirst` requires `gradle.startParameter.isWriteDependencyLocks` (i.e. must be run with `--write-locks`) or fails with "<path> must be run with the --write-locks flag". `doLast` iterates `configurations.filter { it.isCanBeResolved }` and resolves the GRAPH ONLY via `it.incoming.resolutionResult.root` (not artifacts — artifact-variant selection fails for some AGP configurations outside their task context, e.g. app androidTest compile classpath). On exception: if the configuration is in the excludedFromLocking set, log a warning and skip; otherwise rethrow, because any other resolution failure means an incomplete lockfile. Verification contract: `./gradlew resolveAndLockAll --write-locks` must produce no lockfile diff on an unchanged tree. `./gradlew help` does NOT validate lockfile completeness (it resolves nothing).

capabilities.name: Workflow Lint gate — job shape and pinned-binary installs
capabilities.behavior: Workflow `Workflow Lint` (workflow-lint.yml). Triggers: push main/develop; PR main/develop opened|synchronize|reopened; workflow_dispatch. `contents: read`. Concurrency `workflow-lint-${{ github.ref }}`, cancel-in-progress. Job `workflow-lint` / name `Workflow Lint`, ubuntu-latest, `timeout-minutes: 5`. Both tools are installed as version-pinned release tarballs with SHA-256 verification (`sha256sum -c -`) rather than third-party actions, so the gate has no unpinned dependency of its own. shellcheck v0.10.0, sha256 `6c881ab0698e4e6ea235245f22832860544f17ba386442fe7e9d629f8cbedf87`, extracted with `--strip-components=1` into `$RUNNER_TEMP/tools`. actionlint v1.7.7, sha256 `023070a287cd8cccd71515fedc843f1985bf96c436b7effaecce67290e7e0757`, same dir. `$RUNNER_TEMP/tools` appended to GITHUB_PATH.
edge_cases: A tampered or re-cut upstream release tarball fails the sha256sum check and hard-fails the gate.

capabilities.name: actionlint run (guard 1 of 3)
capabilities.behavior: `actionlint -oneline -shellcheck="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/shellcheck"` with no file args — actionlint auto-discovers `.github/workflows/`. Catches unknown/undefined contexts and named-values (the "Unrecognized named-value" class that broke op-load-signing-secrets), malformed expressions, invalid `needs`/`if`, and — via the shellcheck integration — shell bugs inside `run:` blocks. It validates the local composite action's input contract indirectly, through the workflows that call it; it does NOT lint composite action definitions (it parses action.yml as a malformed workflow), which is why guard 3 exists.

capabilities.name: SHA-pin guard (guard 2 of 3)
capabilities.behavior: Enforces that every third-party `uses:` pins a full 40-hex commit SHA — actionlint does not check this, and Renovate/CodeRabbit only advise it. Extraction: `grep -rhE '^[[:space:]]*(-[[:space:]]+)?uses:[[:space:]]' .github/workflows .github/actions | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="uses:"){print $(i+1); break}}'` — awk isolates the whitespace-delimited token after `uses:`, robust to a leading `- `, extra spacing, a trailing `# vX` comment, and trailing whitespace. Per ref: strip surrounding single/double quotes; skip empty, `./*` (local actions) and `docker://*`; if there is no `@` → error "not pinned (no @<sha>)"; else `sha=${ref##*@}` must be length 40 and contain only `0-9a-f` (checked via `tr -d '0-9a-f'` yielding empty). Any failure sets failed=1 and the step exits 1 after listing all offenders. Covers `.github/workflows/**` AND `.github/actions/**`.
edge_cases: A `uses:` written inside a YAML comment would still be extracted (the regex allows leading whitespace and `- ` only, but does not exclude `#`-prefixed lines).

capabilities.name: Composite-action secrets-context guard (guard 3 of 3)
capabilities.behavior: Composite actions cannot read the `secrets` context; a `${{ secrets.* }}` reference inside one resolves to EMPTY at runtime — the exact failure that broke op-load-signing-secrets. Implementation: `grep -rnE '\$\{\{[[:space:]]*secrets\.' .github/actions | grep -vE ':[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*#'` — the second grep excludes comment lines (which legitimately document what the calling job must set). Any surviving hit emits `::error::Composite action uses the secrets context (inherit via env from the calling job instead): <hit>` and the step exits 1. The prescribed alternative is inheriting the value through the calling job's `env:`.
edge_cases: Only excludes comments where `#` is the first non-space char after the line number; a trailing inline comment containing secrets.* would still fail.

capabilities.name: Workflow Security gate — zizmor Medium+ threshold
capabilities.behavior: Workflow `Workflow Security` (workflow-security.yml). Push triggers are paths-filtered to `.github/workflows/**`, `.github/actions/**`, `zizmor.yml`; PR trigger has NO paths filter deliberately, so the required check is always created (a paths-filtered required job stays pending forever and wedges the merge). Concurrency `workflow-security-${{ github.ref }}`. Job name `Workflow Security`, ubuntu-latest, `timeout-minutes: 5`. Setup: checkout persist-credentials false, `actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065` (v5) python 3.12, `pip install zizmor==1.5.2 pyyaml==6.0.2`. Gate: `zizmor --config zizmor.yml --min-severity=medium .github/workflows/ .github/actions/` with `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` (read-only, enables online audits such as known-vulnerable-actions against the advisory DB). Any non-allowlisted Medium+ finding → non-zero exit → check fails. Informational findings are logged only.
edge_cases: Stated policy: known-safe findings are allowlisted one at a time with a rationale in zizmor.yml — NEVER by lowering the --min-severity threshold.

capabilities.name: pull_request_target PR-head-checkout guard (zizmor backstop)
capabilities.behavior: Inline python3 heredoc using PyYAML, run before zizmor. Rationale: zizmor attributes `dangerous-triggers` to the trigger itself and emits no distinct finding for a PR-head checkout, so allowlisting the trigger (whole-file OR line-scoped) would also mask the one real regression — checking out PR-supplied code. Algorithm: glob `.github/workflows/*.yml` + `*.yaml`; `yaml.safe_load`; `trigger_names(doc)` reads `doc.get("on", doc.get(True))` because YAML 1.1 parses a bare `on:` key as boolean True, and normalizes str/list/dict to a set; skip files without `pull_request_target`; for each job's steps where `uses` startswith `actions/checkout`, fail if `with.ref` or `with.repository` is a string containing `github.event.pull_request.head`. Emits `::error file=<path>::` per hit and exits 1. Explicitly NOT airtight — laundering the head ref through a prior step's output evades it; it is a backstop layered with zizmor and CODEOWNERS review.
edge_cases: Only actions/checkout is inspected; a manual `git fetch` of the PR head in a run: block is not detected.
Non-dict YAML documents are skipped silently.

capabilities.name: zizmor.yml allowlist contents
capabilities.behavior: Two rules. `dangerous-triggers` — whole-file ignores for the four pull_request_target workflows: auto-merge-renovate.yml (reads PR file list + labels via API only), renovate-file-scope.yml (PR file list via API only), auto-label.yml (reads PR metadata via API; checks out the BASE ref with persist-credentials false), attribution-check.yml (checks out base ref only; fetches PR commits into a remote-only ref for grep/sed text inspection). Whole-file is intentional because zizmor attributes the finding to the trigger, so line-scoping suppresses identically; the masked regression is covered by the python guard. `artipacked` — LINE-scoped ignores at `changelog-pr.yml:49`, `sync-main-to-develop.yml:43`, `release.yml:154`: these three checkouts persist a scoped App token because they push (changelog branch / sync branch / fallback version bump) and none uploads the checkout or .git as an artifact. Each entry ignores ONE audit id, so a different unsafe construct in the same file still fails, and a NEW file with these patterns is not covered.
edge_cases: The `github-env` finding on op-load-signing-secrets is suppressed INLINE (`run: |  # zizmor: ignore[github-env]`) rather than in zizmor.yml — documented as the mechanism for composite-action findings, robust across zizmor versions and line shifts.
zizmor.yml is CODEOWNERS-gated to @jlengelbrecht precisely because an edit can silently widen what the gate ignores.

capabilities.name: Android Gate — aggregation logic
capabilities.behavior: Workflow `Android` (android.yml). Permissions `contents: read`, `pull-requests: read`. Concurrency `android-${{ github.ref }}`. `detect-changes` (dorny/paths-filter v4.0.2, filter id `android`) → output `should_build`. `build` (name "Build & Test") runs if `should_build == 'true'` or workflow_dispatch: JDK 17 temurin via `actions/setup-java@0f481fcb…` (v5.5.0), `gradle/actions/setup-gradle@3f131e86…` (v6.2.0), then `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest`, `./gradlew lintDebug`, `./gradlew assembleDebug`; uploads `debug-apks` (app + wear-device debug APKs, retention 14 days). `android-gate` (name "Android Gate", `if: always()`, `needs: [detect-changes, build]`) mirrors the dep-gate decision tree: detect-changes non-success → fail; workflow_dispatch → require build success; `should_build != 'true'` → pass as skipped; build success → pass; else fail.
edge_cases: `instrumented-tests` is deliberately NOT in `needs` of android-gate.
No timeout-minutes on the build job.

capabilities.name: Android path filter (includes license documents)
capabilities.behavior: Filter `android` matches: `app/**`, `wear-device/**`, `watchface/**`, `plugins/**`, `gradle/**`, `gradlew`, `gradlew.bat`, `settings.gradle.kts`, `settings-gradle.lockfile`, `build.gradle.kts`, `gradle.properties`, `.github/workflows/android.yml`, plus `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `docs/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md` and `docs/licenses/**`. The document entries are included because they are compiled into the APK as assets and gated by `LicenseAssetsTest` — editing, emptying, or deleting one must re-run the attribution drift gate. Docs/governance-only PRs (CLAUDE.md, other docs/**) skip the build.

capabilities.name: Instrumented Tests (emulator) job — non-required by design
capabilities.behavior: Job `instrumented-tests`, name `Instrumented Tests (emulator)`, gated by the same `should_build` filter, `timeout-minutes: 45`, `permissions: contents: read`, `env.API_LEVEL: 35` (matches the app's targetSdk). Steps: Enable KVM (writes `KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0666", OPTIONS+="static_node=kvm"` to /etc/udev/rules.d/99-kvm4all.rules, then `udevadm control --reload-rules` and `udevadm trigger --name-match=kvm`) → checkout → JDK 17 → setup-gradle → AVD cache restore/create/save → run tests. Test run uses `reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@a421e438…` (v2.38.0) with api-level 35, target google_apis, arch x86_64, force-avd-creation false, emulator-options `-no-snapshot-save -no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect -noaudio -no-boot-anim -camera-back none`, disable-animations true, script `./gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest`.
edge_cases: Explicitly NOT required and NOT folded into Android Gate while it beds in, so a flaky emulator cannot wedge unrelated PRs. Promotion to required is a branch-protection change once it proves stable.
No auto-retry: a red result reflects a real test failure or genuine infra problem; the documented response is to re-run the single job, never to disable the test.

Report uploaded as `instrumented-test-report` (`if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`, retention 14 days, if-no-files-found ignore) from app/build/reports/androidTests/connected/** and app/build/outputs/androidTest-results/connected/**.

capabilities.name: AVD cache state machine
capabilities.behavior: Three states keyed on `avd-v1-${API_LEVEL}-google_apis-x86_64` (paths `~/.android/avd/*`, `~/.android/adb*`). (1) Restore — `actions/cache/restore@55cc8345…` (v6.1.0), id `avd-cache`. (2) On miss (`cache-hit != 'true'`) — Create AVD and generate snapshot via android-emulator-runner with force-avd-creation false, emulator-options `-no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect -noaudio -no-boot-anim -camera-back none`, disable-animations false, script echoes a message. (3) Save — `actions/cache/save@55cc8345…` guarded by `cache-hit != 'true' && success()`, so a cancelled or failed generation skips the save and a partial/corrupt snapshot never poisons the cache. Restore+explicit-save (not the combined cache action) exists specifically for that guard. The `-v1` key prefix is the documented one-line manual eviction path if a bad snapshot lands.

capabilities.name: Bootstrap Check (ci.yml) — App-token plumbing smoke
capabilities.behavior: Workflow `Bootstrap Check`, job `bootstrap-check` / name `App Token Auth + Runner Check`. Triggers push main/develop, PR main/develop (opened|synchronize|reopened), workflow_dispatch. `contents: read`. Mints a short-lived installation token from the org's `glycemicgpt-ci` GitHub App via `actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1` (v3.2.0) using org-level secrets `CI_APP_ID` / `CI_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` (visibility: all, auto-inherited). Both the mint step and the verify step are guarded by `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork != true` — GitHub does not pass org/repo secrets to fork-originated pull_request runs, so the steps would receive empty inputs and crash on the first external contributor's PR. Verify step runs `gh api repos/${{ github.repository }} --jq .name`. A final step just echoes the KVM-runner reminder.
edge_cases: The file's header comment is stale — it claims to be "currently the only workflow in the repository" while 17 others exist.

capabilities.name: Secrets Plumbing Check (1Password canary)
capabilities.behavior: Workflow `Secrets Plumbing Check`, job `canary` / name `Resolve 1Password canary`. `workflow_dispatch` ONLY — never runs on push/PR and never reads a keystore or password. `contents: read`. Concurrency `secrets-plumbing-${{ github.ref }}`. Job env maps `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_ACTIONS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}` (a read-only 1Password service-account token — the only signing-related secret stored in GitHub). Installs `1password/install-cli-action@a5215d3a7f75c1629216c465ea9ab3ab399c4b71` (v4.0.0). Under `set -euo pipefail`: empty token → `::error::` + exit 1; else `op read op://github/android-signing/canary` must succeed and be non-empty → prints "1Password plumbing OK"; failure → `::error::` + exit 1. The resolved value ("ok") is asserted on, never echoed. Dispatchable only once the file reaches the default branch.

capabilities.name: Signing Action Smoke (end-to-end keystore materialization)
capabilities.behavior: Workflow `Signing Action Smoke`, job `smoke` / name `Materialize debug keystore via composite action`. `workflow_dispatch` only; `contents: read`; concurrency `signing-action-smoke-${{ github.ref }}`. Maps `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` at JOB level (the `secrets` context is valid in a workflow file but not inside a composite action) and invokes `./.github/actions/op-load-signing-secrets` with `keystore: debug`. Assertions under `set -euo pipefail`: `DEBUG_KEYSTORE_FILE` must be exported; the action's `keystore-path` output must equal it; the file must exist and be non-empty (`-s`). Only paths are printed — never a keystore byte, password, or the token. Final step `if: always()` runs `rm -f "${{ steps.signing.outputs.keystore-path }}"`. Complements secrets-plumbing-check: that one never touches signing material; this one proves the action both LOADS (passes template validation) and works.

capabilities.name: op-load-signing-secrets composite action (target of both smoke gates)
capabilities.behavior: Input `keystore` (required, must be "release" or "debug"; anything else → `::error::` + exit 1). Preflight also fails if OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN is unset. Installs 1Password CLI v4.0.0 (SHA a5215d3a…), then `1password/load-secrets-action@3a12b0ab99d9cd590a3e9b5a90ea017210ed9556` (v4.0.1) with export-env true resolving text fields RELEASE_/DEBUG_ KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, KEY_ALIAS, KEY_PASSWORD from `op://github/android-signing/<NAME>` — names match app/build.gradle.kts 1:1, no renaming. Materialize step: chooses op ref `release.jks`→`$RUNNER_TEMP/release.jks` (env RELEASE_KEYSTORE_FILE) or `debug.keystore`→`$RUNNER_TEMP/debug.keystore` (DEBUG_KEYSTORE_FILE); `umask 077`, `trap 'rm -f "$dest"' ERR`, `rm -f "$dest"`, `op read --out-file "$dest" --force`, `chmod 600`, writes keystore-path to GITHUB_OUTPUT and the *_KEYSTORE_FILE name to GITHUB_ENV.
edge_cases: `--force` prevents hanging on the overwrite-confirmation prompt on re-runs/self-hosted runners.
umask+delete-before-create ensures the keystore is never briefly group/world-readable; the ERR trap removes a partially written keystore.
Composite actions cannot register a post-job step — on a self-hosted/persistent runner the caller must `rm -f` the keystore itself.
`run: |  # zizmor: ignore[github-env]` is the inline zizmor suppression, justified because the GITHUB_ENV value is a hardcoded $RUNNER_TEMP path selected by the literal input.

capabilities.name: CodeRabbit review posture and gating strength
capabilities.behavior: .coderabbit.yaml (schema v2). `profile: chill`, `request_changes_workflow: true`, `review_status: true`, `commit_status: true`, **`fail_commit_status: false`** — CodeRabbit's commit status does NOT block merge. `abort_on_close: true`. auto_review: enabled, auto_incremental_review true, `auto_pause_after_reviewed_commits: 3`, `drafts: false`, base_branches `[develop]`, title keywords that skip review: WIP, DO NOT MERGE, DRAFT, [skip review]; ignored bot authors: glycemicgpt-renovate[bot], glycemicgpt-release[bot], renovate[bot], dependabot[bot], github-actions[bot]. pre_merge_checks: title/description/issue_assessment in `warning` mode; the three custom checks in `error` mode. finishing_touches docstrings and unit_tests disabled. knowledge_base learnings/issues/pull_requests scope `local`; code_guidelines filePatterns CLAUDE.md and docs/dev/plugin-architecture.md.
edge_cases: Renovate/dependabot/release-bot PRs are NOT reviewed by CodeRabbit — dependency bumps get no medical-safety or secret review from this layer.
`fail_commit_status: false` means even `mode: error` custom checks are advisory with respect to GitHub merge blocking; enforcement relies on human review.

capabilities.name: CodeRabbit custom check: "No Hardcoded Secrets" (mode error)
capabilities.behavior: Verifies no hardcoded secrets, API keys, tokens, HMAC keys, passwords, keystore material, or credentials appear in the code changes. Explicitly checks for: strings that look like API keys or tokens, base64-encoded secrets, .env values committed directly, and private URLs or internal hostnames. Framed as critical severity because this is a medical/health-tech application.

capabilities.name: CodeRabbit custom check: "Medical Safety Review" (mode error) — SAFETY
capabilities.behavior: Applies when a PR touches glucose values, insulin/pump telemetry, or unit conversions. Rules: glucose is STORED and COMPARED in canonical mg/dL; every persisted field, bound, threshold/alert comparison, dedup key, and safety check must stay in mg/dL and be bounds-checked to 20–500 mg/dL. mmol/L is DISPLAY and INPUT only; the single allowed conversion factor is 18.0156 (mg/dL per mmol/L). Hard-FAIL if code (a) stores or compares an mmol/L value as if it were mg/dL (e.g. persisting 3.9 instead of ~70 — explicitly called out as silently suppressing low alerts), (b) converts the wrong direction, (c) permits a stored mg/dL value outside 20–500 after conversion, or (d) uses any factor other than 18.0156. Also: no auto-bolus or therapeutic device-command code may exist; AI-generated suggestions must carry safety disclaimers. Passes if the PR does not touch medical data handling.
edge_cases: Explicit non-violations: a user-facing mmol/L display literal (3.9, 10.0, 22.2) and an mmol/L input converted to mg/dL before storage. Only the stored/compared mg/dL value must be in 20–500.
Test-path instructions name the mmol/L equivalents of the bounds as ~1.1 and ~27.8 mmol/L, again as display literals not bounds violations.

capabilities.name: CodeRabbit custom check: "BLE Protocol Safety" (mode error) — SAFETY
capabilities.behavior: Applies when a PR modifies BLE communication code. Verifies: GATT operations have timeouts and are serialized (one at a time); connection state transitions are handled; byte parsing uses correct endianness (Little Endian for the Tandem protocol); no raw pump data, pump serials, or auth material is logged at INFO level. Passes if the PR does not touch BLE code. The richer `plugins/shipped/**/ble/**` path_instructions add: the connection state machine must handle unexpected disconnect, bond loss, and GATT 133 errors; event type IDs must match the protocol spec; multi-packet characteristic streaming must handle reassembly with the documented idle timeout; DEBUG-level logging only.
edge_cases: The `plugins/shipped/**/ble/**` path rules do NOT cover BLE spikes under tools/ (e.g. tools/medtronic-ble-spike); docs state the semantic BLE Protocol Safety custom check is nonetheless expected to apply there.

capabilities.name: CodeRabbit path_instructions and scope filters
capabilities.behavior: path_instructions cover: `{app,wear-device,watchface}/**/*.kt` (Compose state hoisting/remember/derivedStateOf/testTag, Hilt annotations, Room DAO/migration/type-converters, EncryptedSharedPreferences for tokens, SQLCipher for the DB, no sensitive data in logs, plus the mg/dL 20–500 + 18.0156 medical rules); `plugins/pump-driver-api/**/*.kt` (interface stability, no :app or plugin imports — stdlib/AndroidX/kotlinx only, `PLUGIN_API_VERSION` must be incremented in PluginMetadata.kt on interface change, SafetyLimits KDoc, PluginCapabilityInterface marker, read-only posture: no therapeutic write primitive); `plugins/shipped/{tandem,medtronic}/**/*.kt` (thin delegating capability wrappers, no :app imports, always forward SafetyLimits — never `SafetyLimits()` default, lifecycle onActivated→auto-reconnect / onDeactivated→disconnect / shutdown→full release, apiVersion must match PLUGIN_API_VERSION, monitoring-only); test paths; and `.github/workflows/**` (no hardcoded secrets, SHA-pinned actions, least privilege, no command injection — route untrusted values through env:).
edge_cases: path_filters exclude images (png/jpg/jpeg/gif/svg/ico/webp), `**/build/**`, `**/.gradle/**`, `**/.android/**`, `**/gradle.lockfile`, `settings-gradle.lockfile`, `**/_bmad-output/**` — lockfile changes are NOT reviewed by CodeRabbit (OSV-Scanner covers them).

capabilities.name: CodeRabbit tool matrix
capabilities.behavior: Enabled: detekt, actionlint, shellcheck, yamllint, markdownlint, gitleaks, semgrep, osvScanner, checkov. Explicitly disabled: ruff, eslint, pylint, hadolint (no Python/JS/Docker in this repo). `gitleaks` here is one of the three secret-scanning layers and the stated reason a dedicated in-repo secret-scanning gate was not added. chat: art false, auto_reply true. knowledge_base.web_search enabled, opt_out false. code_generation: KDoc with @param/@return/@throws; generated tests use JUnit 4 + MockK with coroutine test dispatchers.

capabilities.name: GitGuardian / external secret scanning
capabilities.behavior: GitGuardian is described in docs/dev/security-testing.md as running ORG-WIDE at push time as a separate secret scanner — there is no GitGuardian workflow, action, or config in this repository. It appears in-repo only as an allowed bot in attribution-check.yml's `ALLOWED_BOTS` regex (`gitguardian[bot]`). CONTRIBUTING.md:274 states there is no DAST or GitGuardian secret-scanning check defined in this repo's own CI, and that GitGuardian-equivalent coverage is EXPECTED to come from GitHub platform-level Secret Scanning + Push Protection once the repository exists under the GlycemicGPT organization — i.e. it is an assumed-but-unverified external control today.
edge_cases: Three-layer secret coverage on paper (Semgrep p/secrets in-repo, CodeRabbit gitleaks, org-wide GitGuardian) but only the first is enforced by this repo's own CI, and CodeRabbit's commit status is non-failing.

capabilities.name: DECISION: no dedicated secret-scanning gate
capabilities.behavior: Deliberately NOT added. Stated reason: the Security Scan Gate already runs Semgrep's `p/secrets` ruleset over app/, wear-device/, watchface/, plugins/; `gitleaks` runs on every PR through CodeRabbit; and GitGuardian runs org-wide at push time. A third pass over the same tree would add maintenance and noise without new coverage. The `p/secrets` lane is kept because it is free within the existing SAST run and gives an in-repo, PR-blocking signal independent of the external services. No revisit trigger is documented for this decision.

capabilities.name: DECISION: MobSF / APK-artifact SAST declined — with revisit trigger
capabilities.behavior: Evaluated and deliberately declined. Acknowledged as NOT redundant with Semgrep: MobSF operates on the built artifact and covers AndroidManifest.xml posture (exported components, over-broad permissions, debuggable, allowBackup, usesCleartextTraffic, weak network_security_config), packaging/build config (signing scheme, minSdk exposure, insecure library bundling), and secrets embedded in the PACKAGED APK (resources, strings.xml, assets, native libs) that never appear in the source tree. Declined because: monitoring-only read-only app distributed by GitHub side-load rather than Play Store (no pre-launch security report, no store-review threat model); MobSF manifest/permission heuristics are high-false-positive on an app that legitimately needs BLE, location for BLE scanning, and foreground-service permissions; running it means building and scanning an APK on every PR plus maintaining a suppression baseline.
edge_cases: REVISIT TRIGGER (verbatim intent): add an APK/manifest SAST gate if the app is ever distributed via the Play Store, OR if ANY write/therapeutic surface (bolus, basal, pump-setting, or other device-command capability) is introduced.
Accepted residual gap, stated explicitly: secrets embedded only in the built artifact (not in source) are NOT scanned today.

Compensating controls named: Android Lint in the Android Gate covers manifest/network-security posture defensively, plus CodeRabbit review; source-level secrets covered by Semgrep p/secrets + gitleaks + GitGuardian; no signing material is committed.

capabilities.name: DECISION: monorepo security lanes not ported
capabilities.behavior: Of the platform monorepo's multi-language security CI, only Android SAST (Semgrep), dependency CVE scanning (OSV over Gradle lockfiles), and secret scanning apply here; workflow hardening (Workflow Lint / Workflow Security) is treated as a separate concern. Not ported because they target a running server/API/web app that does not exist and would be perpetually red: Semgrep Python/TypeScript (no backend/web code); DAST / ZAP / nuclei / the Docker test stack from security-full-suite.yml (no HTTP service; BLE protocol fuzzing needs pump hardware and is out of CI scope); auth pentests (test-auth-flows.py) and API fuzzing (fuzz-api.py, self-adapting via /openapi.json) — marked N/A, no authenticated server or HTTP API surface; evaluate-sast.py + create-finding-issues.py — the issue-filing pipeline depends on the org SECURITY GitHub App and a scripts/security/ Python toolchain this mobile-only repo does not carry, replaced by the plain exit-non-zero-on-HIGH check.
edge_cases: Findings surface only via the run log, the semgrep-kotlin artifact, and CodeRabbit — no auto-filed issues, no tracking, no SLA.

Local SAST repro omits `tools/`; local dep-scan repro omits `--no-ignore`.

capabilities.name: Fork-PR behavior of the security gates
capabilities.behavior: security-scan.yml, workflow-lint.yml, workflow-security.yml, android.yml and dependency-scan.yml all use plain `pull_request`, so they run on fork PRs with a read-only token and no secrets — none of them needs a secret. ci.yml's App-token steps are explicitly skipped for fork PRs (`github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork != true`) because GitHub withholds org/repo secrets from fork pull_request runs. Workflows that need write access (attribution-check, auto-label, renovate-file-scope, auto-merge-renovate) use `pull_request_target` in base-repo context and are individually allowlisted in zizmor.yml; none checks out PR head code. CONTRIBUTING.md states every required check runs automatically for fork PRs with no maintainer action needed. The two 1Password workflows are workflow_dispatch-only and therefore never fork-reachable.
edge_cases: CodeRabbit has its own review queue; stale state on a fast-pushing PR is not a CI failure. `@coderabbitai review` re-triggers.

capabilities.name: CODEOWNERS as a security control
capabilities.behavior: `/.github/workflows/` → @jlengelbrecht (project-lead review required on every workflow change, because workflow files run with secret access and, for bypass-actor bots, write access to protected branches). `/zizmor.yml` → @jlengelbrecht, explicitly because a careless edit can "silently widen what the Workflow Security gate ignores". Also lead-owned: SECURITY.md, .github/dco.yml, CODEOWNERS, GOVERNANCE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, release.yml, renovate.json5, release-please config/manifest, changelog-pr-config.json, autolabeler-config.json, gradle/libs.versions.toml, and the safety-critical driver paths /plugins/pump-driver-api/, /plugins/shipped/tandem/, /plugins/shipped/medtronic/. capabilities.name: Mobile security measures verification matrix
capabilities.behavior: docs/dev/security-testing.md maps each control to its verifier: SQLCipher database encryption → unit tests + CodeRabbit review; EncryptedSharedPreferences for tokens → unit tests + CodeRabbit review; HTTPS enforcement (network_security_config) → Android Lint + CodeRabbit review; no sensitive data in logs → CodeRabbit BLE Protocol Safety check; dependency vulnerabilities → OSV-Scanner recursive Gradle scan; hardcoded secrets → Semgrep p/secrets + CodeRabbit gitleaks + org-wide GitGuardian; insecure code patterns → Semgrep SAST (p/kotlin, p/java, p/secrets); medical safety / conversion correctness → CodeRabbit Medical Safety Review check. Explicit statement: no DAST scanning for mobile — BLE protocol fuzzing would require hardware and is out of CI scope.
edge_cases: Two of the eight rows ("no sensitive data in logs", "medical safety / conversion correctness") have CodeRabbit as their ONLY verifier — and CodeRabbit's commit status is configured non-failing.

capabilities.name: Adding security coverage for a new plugin
capabilities.behavior: Auto-covered: Android Gate (plugins/** is in the detect-changes filter, so build/test/lint runs); SAST (Kotlin/Java plugin code is inside the Semgrep scan roots); dependency scan (a new module's gradle.lockfile is picked up by the recursive sweep once the module joins the build — lockfiles must be regenerated after adding dependencies). Only manual action required: if a plugin introduces a new auth or pairing flow, add coverage in that plugin's own test suite — there is no shared auth-flow test harness in this repo (unlike the backend API).

safety_critical: Glucose bounds are encoded ONLY as CI review policy, not as executable CI checks: canonical storage/comparison unit mg/dL, valid range 20–500 mg/dL, single allowed conversion factor 18.0156 mg/dL per mmol/L. Enforced by the CodeRabbit "Medical Safety Review" custom check (.coderabbit.yaml:210-234) and the {app,wear-device,watchface}/**/*.kt path_instructions. No Semgrep rule, unit test, or gradle check in this subsystem enforces them.

Named failure mode with patient impact, verbatim from .coderabbit.yaml: persisting an mmol/L value as if it were mg/dL (e.g. storing 3.9 instead of ~70) SILENTLY SUPPRESSES LOW ALERTS. Also hard-fail: converting the wrong direction, permitting a stored mg/dL value outside 20–500 after conversion, or using any factor other than 18.0156.

Explicit non-violations that must not be 'fixed': user-facing mmol/L display literals (3.9, 10.0, 22.2; test-path doc names ~1.1 and ~27.8 mmol/L as the display equivalents of the 20/500 bounds), and mmol/L input converted to mg/dL before storage.

Monitoring-only, read-only posture is a safety and legal boundary enforced by review only: no auto-bolus, no bolus/basal/pump-setting write, no therapeutic device command may exist on any capability interface (SECURITY.md, .coderabbit.yaml pump-driver-api and shipped-driver path_instructions). SECURITY.md states a report proposing to add write capability will be declined.

Introducing ANY write/therapeutic surface is a documented revisit trigger for adding APK/manifest SAST (docs/dev/security-testing.md:107-110) — i.e. the current security-gate design is calibrated to the read-only threat model and must be re-derived if that changes.

BLE protocol correctness is gated only by the CodeRabbit "BLE Protocol Safety" check: GATT ops serialized and timed out; connection state machine handles unexpected disconnect, bond loss, GATT 133; Little Endian for the Tandem protocol; event type IDs match the protocol spec; multi-packet reassembly honors the documented idle timeout. No CI tool verifies any of this.
Never log raw pump data, pump serials, or auth material at INFO level (DEBUG only). Verified solely by CodeRabbit review per the security-testing.md matrix.
SafetyLimits must always be forwarded to the underlying BLE driver/parser; `SafetyLimits()` defaults are forbidden in shipped drivers. Review-only enforcement.

CodeRabbit `fail_commit_status: false` means the three `mode: error` custom checks — including Medical Safety Review and BLE Protocol Safety — do NOT block a merge via GitHub status. The only hard-blocking safety control is human CODEOWNERS review on /plugins/pump-driver-api/, /plugins/shipped/tandem/, /plugins/shipped/medtronic/.
CodeRabbit skips PRs authored by renovate/dependabot/release/github-actions bots, so dependency-bump PRs receive no medical-safety or BLE review from that layer.

Dependency Scan Gate PASSES without scanning on any PR that does not touch a dependency-relevant path; a newly disclosed CVE in an unchanged dependency is caught only by the Monday 06:00 UTC cron or a manual dispatch.
Instrumented Tests (emulator) — which executes the Room migration test and Compose/espresso UI tests — is deliberately NOT a required check, so a PR can merge with those tests red.
Semgrep p/kotlin/p/java/p/secrets rule packs are fetched from the registry at scan time even though the CLI is pinned to 1.169.0: the effective SAST policy is not reproducible from the repo alone.
Semgrep records unparseable files in .errors[] without changing its exit code; a Kotlin file that fails to parse yields zero findings and still passes the gate (surfaced as a ::warning:: only).
Accepted residual gap, stated in docs: secrets embedded only in the BUILT ARTIFACT (APK resources, strings.xml, assets, native libs) are not scanned today by anything.

STRUCTURAL OBSERVATIONS a rebuild must preserve:
- The "always report" pattern is load-bearing: a required check that is paths-filtered at the workflow level never gets created and leaves the PR pending forever. Two workflows solve this differently — security-scan/workflow-security run unconditionally on every PR; android/dependency-scan use an `if: always()` aggregation job that reads `needs.*.result` through `env:` and treats "skipped because nothing relevant changed" as a pass.
- Fail-closed is implemented in exactly two places: the Semgrep `SEMGREP_EXIT >= 2` check (with `:-2` default so an unset value also fails) and the aggregation jobs' non-success branches.
- The Workflow Lint / Workflow Security split is deliberate: syntax+shell vs security posture. Three guards exist because actionlint cannot lint composite-action definitions and does not check SHA pinning, and zizmor cannot distinguish a safe pull_request_target from a PR-head checkout.
- Suppression discipline is a stated invariant across all three config files: never lower a threshold, always allowlist one finding at a time with a written reason (zizmor.yml whole-file vs line-scoped choice is itself justified per entry; osv-scanner.toml requires a `reason` and prefers an `ignoreUntil`; Semgrep has no baseline mechanism at all).
- osv-scanner.toml currently has ZERO active suppressions and zizmor.yml has 7 (4 dangerous-triggers whole-file, 3 artipacked line-scoped) plus 1 inline `# zizmor: ignore[github-env]` in the composite action.
